# Collections

RObjC provides three collection families for `RSObject` instances. Each has a
read-only class and a mutable class. Choose the family by how elements are
found, then choose whether the collection's membership or order may change.

| Family | Read-only | Mutable | Main behavior |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Array | `RSArray` | `RSMutableArray` | Ordered elements, one-based indices |
| Dictionary | `RSDictionary` | `RSMutableDictionary` | Values found by key |
| Set | `RSSet` | `RSMutableSet` | Unique members, no defined order |

The read-only classes reject changes to the collection. `copy()` on a
read-only collection returns that same instance; `mutableCopy()` creates an
editable collection. On a mutable collection, `copy()` creates a read-only
collection and `mutableCopy()` creates a separate mutable one. These copies
are shallow: stored objects can still be shared.

## Array: position matters

Arrays store RObjC objects in order. `objectAtIndex()` uses R-style one-based
indices. A mutable array can append, insert, replace, and remove elements.

```{r}
library(robjc)

array <- RSArray_withObjects(list(
  RSString_withValue("first"),
  RSString_withValue("second")
))
stopifnot(identical(array$objectAtIndex(2L)$value(), "second"))

editable_array <- array$mutableCopy()
editable_array$addObject(RSString_withValue("third"))
stopifnot(identical(array$count(), 2L))
stopifnot(identical(editable_array$count(), 3L))
```

Use `asList()` to obtain a regular R list of the stored objects. An array's
order and repeated elements are retained.

## Dictionary: keys identify values

Dictionaries map RObjC keys to RObjC values. Search with `objectForKey()` or
check presence with `containsKey()`. Key lookup uses `hash()` and `isEqual()`,
so a separate but equal key can find the value.

```{r}
dictionary <- RSDictionary_withObjectForKey(
  RSNumber_withValue(10L),
  RSString_withValue("id")
)
stopifnot(dictionary$containsKey(RSString_withValue("id")))
stopifnot(identical(
  dictionary$objectForKey(RSString_withValue("id"))$value(), 10L
))
```

Dictionary order is unspecified. Insertion calls the key's `copy()`; the
key's hash and equality state must remain stable while stored. See
`vignette("robjc_dictionary", package = "robjc")` for `NULL` values,
key behavior, and copy semantics.

## Set: unique membership

Sets keep one member for each equality class and have no defined iteration
order. Membership uses each object's `hash()` and `isEqual()`. A mutable set
can add and remove members; `uniteSet()`, `intersectSet()`, and
`subtractSet()` return new read-only sets.

```{r}
set <- RSSet_withObjects(list(
  RSString_withValue("a"),
  RSString_withValue("a"),
  RSString_withValue("b")
))
stopifnot(set$count() == 2)
stopifnot(set$containsObject(RSString_withValue("a")))

editable_set <- set$mutableCopy()
editable_set$addObject(RSString_withValue("c"))
stopifnot(set$count() == 2)
stopifnot(editable_set$count() == 3)
```

Sets retain inserted objects rather than copying them. Keep a member's hash
and equality state stable while it belongs to a set. R `NULL` is represented
by `RSNull$null` in sets and dictionaries.
